1.title: Borealis Order 1 - pneumatics, electronics, speakers
rows: PRESSURE SIDE - tanks, rear manifold, main valve and in valves (200 psi)
Air tank 6 L / 1.6 gal, 200 psi, 1/4 NPT, aluminum (your pick)
Two, 12 L: left and right over the front wheels. The CAD test-fit found no room for a third alongside them; 9-15 shots at 120 ft per 150-200 psi charge with a fast top valve, 6-10 with a slow one
Relief valve 200 psi, 1/4 NPT male, ASME, ring pull, brass, 2-pack (Loner ST25-1A200, B0F4QP9CG2)
Tank zone (rear manifold; its ring at the rear panel is the hand dump), the valve cross, and the cross after each in valve on the chassis (its ring is that chamber's bleed)

Claude: no. This is a compressor pop-off with no ASME stamp (2 for $9.99). The relief is the last line of defense, more so with welded chambers, and the ASME McMaster ones cost only about $7 more for all four.
Pressure transducer 0-300 psi, 0.5-4.5 V, 5 V, 1/8 NPT, stainless, with plug cable (pick "1set-300PSI")

One part number for all three: the tank, and one per chamber on the chassis cross after its in valve (Brophy Borealis compact gun), so no sensor wires cross the pivot. Fill in short pulses and read between them: the hose reads a little high while air is flowing. +$1.99 shipping
Claude: yes, switching to this one. Pick "1set-300PSI": $6.08 with its plug cable, +$1.99 shipping. Same 1/8 NPT thread and 0.5-4.5 V output. The $1.09 price is a one-time new-shopper offer.
Quick disconnects: 1/4 NPT female M-style couplers, brass, 300 psi, 5-pack (RUBY.Q B0BPXT6V2F)

The 5 interior quick disconnects: tank line to the main valve, rear manifold to each in valve (2), each chassis cross to its chamber hose (2). Couplers have the shut-off, so they go on the supply side; the fifth threads straight onto the port that the old kit's F x F coupling + male-thread coupler sat on

Claude: no. The seller's description says 150 psi max, and the fittings are aluminum; these see 190-200 psi. Replacing this row and both Milton rows with the Lnrueg 45-piece M-style kit (Amazon B0G6YF5J3L, $27.98, rated 300 psi): 4 + 4 couplers, 14 + 14 plugs, and F x F couplings. Saves about $22.
QD plugs + fill plug: 1/4 NPT FEMALE-thread M-style plugs, brass, 10 pcs (ZKZX B081F9J3VF, pick 'Female NPT')
6 used: the fill plug outside the rear panel (on the 1-1/2 in nipple; your universal couplers snap on) and one per interior QD. Still an open plug, so the check valve behind it stays
Fill check valve, 304 stainless, 1/4 NPT male x male (your AliExpress pick)

Behind the panel, between the female elbow and the street elbow. Holds the tanks shut when the hose comes off (the plug is an open pipe). No pressure rating listed, so leak-test it at 200 psi with soapy water
Claude: yes, switching to this one (about $7.36, 304 stainless, 1/4 NPT male x male). It lists no pressure rating, so leak-test it at 200 psi with soapy water.
In valves: GOGO GPG-M03 2/2 NC direct-acting 12 V DC, G1/4 (BSPP), 2.5 mm, 0-35 bar (option 1/4", DC12V, 2.5mm 35bar)

One in valve per chamber, metering it against the transducer on its chassis cross; they hold tank pressure all session. G1/4 ports: a G1/4 x 1/4 NPT adapter with a bonded seal in each (rows below). Flow arrow toward the chamber; soap-test at 200 psi

Claude: no. That valve (liyadu CS-08, 16 bar, $25.70) only comes with G1/4 (BSP) threads, and so does every other high-pressure valve I found on AliExpress. Four BSP-to-NPT adapters cost about $20, which leaves about $9 of the $31 saving. Keeping the Aignep.
Adapters: G1/4 BSPP male x 1/4 NPT male hex nipple, 304 stainless (pick "G1/4 BSPP / 1/4 NPT / Male to male")
Both ports of both in valves: inlet to its QD plug, outlet to its chassis cross. They take the place of 4 close nipples. Bonded seal on the G1/4 side, sealant on the NPT side only
Bonded seals: self-centering NBR, 14 mm (fits G1/4), 20 pcs (pick "14mm")
One under each adapter's hex at the in valve ports (4 of 20): G1/4 is a parallel thread, so it seals on the face, not the thread
Rear manifold, the valve cross, and one on the chassis right after each in valve: its chamber's transducer, relief and hose out (moved off the gun, Brophy Borealis)
1/4 NPT brass close nipple, 5-pack, 250 psi (FLOFLEX B0CRVX12WC)

2 used (CAD count, Brophy Borealis): one joining the rear manifold's two port blocks, one between the main valve's street elbow and the ball valve. The in valves' ports take the G1/4 adapters, which screw straight into the valve cross and the chamber crosses, so one pack is enough (3 spare)
1/4 NPT brass 90 deg elbow, FNPT x FNPT, 2-pack (ChillWaves B0B7544Y62)
Fill line behind the panel: the nipple in one side, the male x male check valve in the other (1 spare)
1/4 NPT brass street elbow 90 deg, MNPT x FNPT, 2 pcs (CX Wonderland B0BCZFCFQ7)
2 used: main valve off the rear manifold, and the check valve into the rear manifold
1/4 NPT plug, 304 stainless, hex socket, 10 pcs (Neprift B0H6X8VCSZ)
Every open port (rev D.2 audit): 2 rear-manifold ends + up to 3 spare bungs per tank (photos show 3-4 ports; one is the outlet) = 8 of 10. The valve cross and the chassis crosses have no open port
1/4 NPT male x 1/8 NPT female hex bushing, brass, 5 pcs (Litoexpe B0BFW3Q864)
DOT nylon air-brake tube 1/4 in OD, SAE J844 PA12, 35 ft, with cutter (Boeray B0CYFWGSYS)
Every air line, including the two service loops to the gun (about 15 ft used)
DOT push-to-connect 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT male, straight, 10-pack (Boeray)

16 used: both halves of the 5 quick disconnects (10), rear manifold (2), main valve, valve cross, and the hose out of each chassis cross (2). One row now: the quick-disconnect row was the same listing
is this teh same as line 11?
Claude: yes, same listing. Merged into this row, qty 2 (16 used).
DOT push-to-connect swivel elbow 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT, 5-pack (Boeray)
4 used: the two tank outlets and the two chamber inlets (in the weld-on bungs, pointing at the pivot); 1 spare
do we need both elbows and normal? can you check quantities?
Claude: yes, both. Straights where the tube runs straight out of a port, elbows where it has to turn right at the port (tank outlets, chamber inlets). Checked: 16 straight, 4 elbows.
Pipe thread sealant, RectorSeal T Plus 2 (B0002YPAFY)
GUN - welded 3 in pipe chambers (Brophy Borealis): top 1.56 L, bottom 1.32 L, both on HSV04 valves to 190 psi; 36 in barrels
Firing valves: U.S. Solid USS-HSV04, 1 in NPT, 12 V DC, NC, pilot-operated, 1-50 bar (725 psi), PTFE seal (Amazon B0BSNHJ4WQ)
One per cannon (rev D.2: the bottom one too, so both run to full tank pressure, capped at 190 under the 200 psi reliefs)

Claude: switched to Amazon. Same U.S. Solid 1 in 12 V DC 50 bar valve, $106.99 each with free delivery, sold by a third-party shop ("The highest quality shop"), so $8.80 more per valve than ussolid.com. (My earlier "no" was about the AliExpress Acarps valve that was linked here before.)
Chamber end plates: 3/8 in A36 hot-rolled steel, 4 x 16 in (B08C2FD1QH)

Waterjet four 3.5 in discs, flush with the pipe: each front disc gets a 1.33 in hole for its outlet nipple, the back discs are blank. Bevel the pipe ends 37.5 deg and weld all the way through. 3/8 in is about twice the thickness 200 psi needs
Claude: yes, welded with flat plates (your pick). Replaces the four MSI couplings ($111.80).
Chambers: 3 in Sch 40 steel pipe, plain end, 24 in (A500, B0FLF5VJMG)

Cut 12.9 in for the top chamber (about 1.56 L) and 10.9 in for the bottom (about 1.32 L). Water-test each welded chamber to 300 psi for 10 minutes before it holds air (borrow a hand test pump and a 0-600 psi gauge). A steel-yard drop works too if it's cheaper
Chamber inlets: 1/4 NPT female steel weld-on step bung, 2-pack (B0H6VR9N6R)
One per chamber on the pipe wall about 1 in behind the front plate, facing the pivot side, so the inlet and outlet are at the same end. A swivel push-to-connect elbow screws in
1 in NPT close nipple (1-1/2 in), seamless steel, Sch 80, ASTM A106, 300 psi (Grainger-approved B007IBN8T4)
Each firing valve to its breech adapter (the chamber side is now the welded nipple in the next row)
would in welded on the tank side if we weld
Claude: yes. The chamber side is now welded (next row); these two stay between each valve and its breech adapter.
Chamber outlets: 1 in x 4 in black steel pipe nipple (LDR 300 1X4, B0002YV7GU)
Cut in half: each cut end is welded through its chamber's front plate, and the HSV04 screws onto the threaded end

Cuts the 1 in NPT threads inside the two aluminum breech adapters (stash 6061 bar). A breech adapter sits right in front of each firing valve: the valve's nipple screws into its back, the barrel slips over its front spigot, and the printed breech block clamps the barrel on
can you elaborate on where the breach adapters are?, also should we weld or tap the connectors?
Claude: tap them. They're aluminum, which can't be welded to the steel nipple, and they only hold pressure for the instant of a shot.
MOSFET switch module 5-36 V 15 A, 3.3-20 V trigger, 10-pack (B0GGHY11RL)

6 used in this order: firing valves (2), in valves (2), and the contactor coil twice in series (one channel for the main controller, one for the safety node). The light bar and smoke get their own pack in Order 2
Barrels: clear extruded polycarbonate tube 3.00 in OD x 2.75 ID x 1/8 wall x 36 in (K-mac B09NLCGBWB)
Two 36 in barrels as they come. Six smoke holes each
ELEVATION - 312 rpm FTC motor on a Spark MAX (backdrives when off), pot for the angle
goBILDA 16T pinion to the printed 112T pivot pulley (CAD loop is exactly 750 mm)
CONTROLS, FAILSAFE + POWER - back bottom bay
Anderson SB50 flush-mount bracket + dust cover kit
Standby charge / shore-power port, bottom of the rear panel (a stash SB50 housing goes in it)
Main controller: Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT, ESP32-P4 + ESP32-C6 (B0FDWZ6KWT)

One board does it all (rev D.2.1): web UI and WebSocket on 2.4 GHz WiFi 6 (the C6 on the board), valves and chamber metering, elevation loop, every LED strip, audio mixing out of its own speaker amp into the siren amp, MIPI camera later, lidar on a UART, the PDH contactor and both battery relays. 5 V from the logic rail on its SH1.0 power header

#1: the three pressure transducers + the 5 V reference. #2: battery A, battery B, the bus and the PDH volts, so the battery relays compare the two packs to a few mV. Both on I2C to the main controller (its own ADC only reads the pot)

12 of 16 used: drive PWM to the 4 Falcons and the elevation Spark MAX, fog heater (2), pump, blower, light bar, both battery relays. Valves, LED data and the contactor stay on the board's own pins (timing and safety). OE is pulled up and held low by the controller, so a reset or crash turns every output off
LED data only now: 3.3 -> 5 V for 8 strip lanes (2 chips). The PWM safety gate is gone (rev D.2): the contactor is the cut-off
12 V 40 A relay with pre-wired socket
Valve arm relay (valve rail, fed from the PDH); flyback diode on the coil. The two fog relays are in Order 2
Relay coils from 3.3 V logic: the valve arm relay, both battery relays and the two fog relays (0.15 A coils; COM to +12 V clamps the flyback)
Contactor + battery relays: 12 V 200 A continuous duty, isolated coil, 4-pin (B0D97PSZBB)

1: the power cut-off between the main breaker and the PDH. Its coil runs through the rear E-stop, the safety node's switch and the main controller's MOSFET in series, so any one of them kills drive, valves, LEDs, audio and fog. 2: one in each battery's + lead, between its SB50 and the shared bus; the controller keeps only the fuller pack connected until the other is within 0.3 V, so a fresh battery never dumps 20-40 A into a flat one
Battery relay bypass: 4.7 ohm 5 W cement resistor, 10-pack (B0FG25KG8C)
One across each battery relay (2 used): feeds the logic rail and boots the controller while both relays are open (power-up, or a dead controller), and trickle-balances the packs at well under 1 A
Logic supply: 5 V 5 A buck-boost, 3.6-32 V in (diymore)
Always-on 5 V logic rail, tapped ahead of the contactor: main controller (its 5 V header), safety node, every sensor
Rear panel: one contact in the contactor coil (kills the PDH), the other in the valve arm relay coil; + the handheld remote
USB to the main controller through the rear panel
Safety remote: 18650 battery shield V8 (charging, 5 V out) + a stash 18650 cell
Remote power, charged over USB, inside your custom printed remote case
AUDIO - two siren speakers in the front corners (replaces the horn)
Siren speaker 200 W, 8 ohm, 121-130 dB, aluminium, 5.7 x 5.5 x 2.3 in (Xprite B01DMSR4L4)
One high in each front-side corner, in a printed cup, aimed 45 deg out and 30 deg up; its L foot bolts through the cup
TPA3255 2 x 300 W class-D amp board, 19-50 V DC, 122 x 73 x 30 mm
One channel per speaker; about 70 W each into 8 ohm on 33 V
1200 W 20 A boost converter, 8-60 V in, 12-80 V out (set to 33 V; pick the "1200W 20A" option)

Feeds the amp from a 40 A PDH channel. At 33 V the amp tops out near 70 W per speaker (about 2 dB under 100 W), so the board stays under the 15 A where the listing asks for extra cooling. The $1.09 price on the listing is a one-time new-shopper offer
ALREADY HAVE - owned or FRC stash, $0, nothing to buy
Main valve: 1/4 NPT brass ball valve, FNPT x FNPT, 600 WOG (the old cannon's if it fits)
Manual tank shut-off (rev C.3): open for a session, closed for transport and before working on the gun; handle at the rear panel
1/4 NPT brass nipple 1-1/2 in (you think you have one)
Through the rear panel: the female plug outside, the female elbow inside. A check valve's 10 mm male end is too short to cross the panel itself
goBILDA 5203-2402-0019 Yellow Jacket 19.2:1 (312 rpm), 8 mm REX (owned)
16T -> 112T belt to the right pivot stub (7:1, about 45 rpm free at the gun, 16.7 N*m stall)
Drives the goBILDA in brushed mode from PWM
The gun angle: on the end of the left pivot stub through its printed coupler, read by the controller (ADS1115)
One per side on its own slide-out sled, each through its own battery relay (below)
REV PDH + ATO breakers, 120 A main breaker, SB50s, wire and lugs
1: safety node (ESP-NOW to the remote; holds the PDH contactor in only while the remote and the main controller are alive). 2: spare
Inline ATO fuse holder + 5 A fuse
Logic tap, right after the main breaker
Resistors and caps (kit): ADC dividers, pull-downs, RC filters
Three transducers (10k/15k), battery A, battery B, bus and PDH volts (39k/10k), 100k pull-downs so a cut sensor wire reads as a fault, the speaker tap
Safety remote: ESP32-C3 SuperMini (one of yours)
Handheld E-stop (the second mushroom above) plus a status LED that shows the link is up; ESP-NOW to the safety node
One per wheel, plain PWM from the main controller (no gate: the contactor is the cut-off)
Old 9 in mecanum wheels (owned, for now)
Stand-ins for the printed 10 in vector wheels (Micah, 2026-11-04); belts and hubs depend on how they mount
2 per wheel axle (inner + outer rail), 4 at the pivot
1/2 in hex shaft: 4 wheel axles (6 in) + 2 pivot stubs
Live axles tapped 10-32 both ends; one steel stub per cradle plate on the pivot axis
Speaker tap: 2 x 1k + 2 x 10 nF low-pass + 1 uF cap (from the kit)

Replaces the PCM5102A: one wire of the board's speaker output (SPK+) through a two-stage 1k/10 nF low-pass and a 1 uF cap into the TPA3255's input (L and R together). Volume and mix are set in software; the amp's gain pot sets the top end
Cup lines each corner notch, 4 x M4 x 8 through its walls into the frame; the speaker's foot bolts through it; grille: 3 walls, no top/bottom layers, 12% gyroid

notes.B5: 200 psi, 1/4 NPT female bungs (photos: 2 along the side, one in an end); it ships with welded feet the CAD saddles ignore. $56.60 list; a $46.81 welcome deal shows for new shoppers. 4.9 stars, 90 sold (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B6: ASME, 200 psi set, 1/4 MNPT, stainless pull ring, 178 cfm; was McMaster 48435K72 4 x $6.67 (Amazon/Ali only, Micah 2026-11-10). Only 8 packs left (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B7: Universal 5 V sender, 30-1000 psi options, connector included; 3K+ sold, 4.8 stars, $10.69 (2026-11-09, L). Was the FUSCH on Amazon at $17.69 each (B0CRQWKDNC). Check the 0.5-4.5 V output on the option page before ordering
notes.B8: 300 psi working; with the plugs below replaces the $27.98 Lnrueg 45-pc kit (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B9: Kenzo's pick was the Male NPT option, which doesn't thread onto the nipples; no psi on the listing (the couplers are the 300 psi parts) (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B10: Male on both ends (listing photo), not FNPT x MNPT as the old note hoped. 250 psi, 250 F, fluorocarbon O-rings, brass. Fit it with the flow arrow pointing in (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B11: GOGO Automatic Company Ltd. (GOGO's own store), 290 sold. $18.22 each + $12.01 shipping split over the two, logged-in price. Brass, NBR seal, DIN plug; body 40 x 26 mm, 76 mm tall, 82 mm long with the plug, 2 x M5 x 8 mounting holes underneath. Coil power not listed (likely 15-20 W: fine on its 15 A MOSFET channel). Replaces the Aignep 02F ($41.36 at Hose Warehouse, 2 mm), Micah's pick (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B12: China Pneumatic Factory Store, 386 sold. $1.77 each + $5.69 shipping split over the four, logged-in price (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B13: SOREKARA, 317 sold, 5.0 stars. $2.78 + $1.99 shipping; the $1.09 it shows is a new-shopper price (2026-11-10, L)
notes.B15: 250 psi rated, 1/4 MNPT both ends; was Legines $7.99 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B16: 1/4 NPT female both ends, barstock brass, 1,200 psi; now $6.39, only 8 left (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B17: Brass, 1/4 MNPT x 1/4 FNPT; no psi on the listing (the old 5-pack had none either); was $11.99 for 5 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B18: 8 used, 2 spare; one 10-pack instead of two brass 5-packs ($15.98) (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B19: 1200 psi rated; was McMaster 9151K91 3 x $2.16 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B20: 500 psi working, 4.35 mm ID; 10 ft more than the old 25 ft roll for less (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B21: 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT male, 250 psi, SAE J1131 + J844, brass; 18 left (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B22: 1/4 tube x 1/4 NPT male, 250 psi, SAE J1131 (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B23: Skip it if you have pipe dope or PTFE tape (Home Depot's $4.25 isn't one of your sellers) (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B24: Free shipping; 12 sold, 5 stars. Was $8.99 on Amazon (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B26: In stock, one version only. Thread is listed as NPT / G (a dual thread, no option to pick), so true NPT is NOT confirmed: test-fit a 1 in NPT nipple before trusting it at 190 psi. Cv 11.67, 25 mm, PTFE seal, junction box. Opening time unpublished: bench-test before cutting barrels (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B27: Same class as the Supply Giant one ("up to 150 lb" on Amazon), but this listing states a 150-300 psi working rating (ASME B16.3 gives Class 150 malleable 300 psi up to 150 F); NPT per ASME B1.20.1. Not one of your sellers; shipping not checked. Cheaper, same Class 150 malleable: Supply Giant CNSD5003 $23.99 on Amazon (B016F1LPTW), saves about $16: kept MSI because you picked it in D.2 for its stated rating; your call (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B28: 3 MNPT both ends, Sch 40 black steel; the listing states no psi (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B29: 1/4-18 NPT, collar OD 24.8 mm x 16.5 mm (the CAD draws the 22 mm AC Performance one: drill the pipe to this one's step); only 15 left (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B30: Sch 80: same 1.315 in OD (no CAD change), bore 24.3 mm vs 26.6 mm, about the HSV04's own orifice; the only Sch 40 ones on Amazon are 150 psi decorative pipe. Was McMaster 44615K416 2 x $3.13 (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B32: Borrow one if the shop has it. 4.6 stars (2026-11-02, S)
notes.B33: Triggers from 3.3 V, so the controller drives them directly (no buffer). Flyback diode across each valve coil; was two 6-packs $10.98 (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B34: Same tube as McMaster 8585K38 ($66.05), free delivery; only 2 left. No pressure rating (none published at McMaster either); clamp it. Not acrylic: it shatters (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B36: 9 mm to match goBILDA's HTD pulleys (AliExpress only has 10 mm); was $8.99 at WCP (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B39: Micah picked it 2026-11-09 over the WTDKP4C5-S1 ($29.29) for the USB plugs: 4 USB-A + 2 USB-C, RJ45 (PoE header), a 40-pin Pi-style header with 28 GPIO (takes Pi HATs), ES8311 codec + NS4150B 2 W speaker amp + mic, speaker included. 2.4 GHz only, so the access point runs 2.4 GHz. Sold by UeeKKoo, 3.6 stars (10); Waveshare store $19.99 + shipping, AliExpress from $27.89 (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B40: Settled call: ESP32 ADCs are too nonlinear for pressure. Two for the price of the single (B0FLPZMQJY, $7.99); 5 stars (3), 50+ bought last month (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B41: The 28 header pins can't take all ~38 D.2 signals; this frees 12. One PWM frequency for all 16 (about 200 Hz suits the Falcons, Spark MAX and light bar; on/off loads use full-on/full-off). 4.5 stars (104), 200+ bought last month (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B43: 4-pin option; 211 sold. Replaces the Nilight 5-pack ($12.14) and the Gebildet 2-pack ($7.99) (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B45: 200 A continuous, 4-pin; only 8 left (3 needed); was $12.99 B07T48QKQB (2026-11-10, Kenzo's list, re-checked L)
notes.B46: Under 1 W each in the worst case: a fresh and a flat pack, one relay open, full drive load. 5 stars (7) (2026-11-09, L)
notes.B47: $2.57 + $5.60 shipping. Short-circuit, over-temperature and TVS protection; holds 5 V down to 3.6 V in, so a drive sag can't reset the controllers. Was the PM02 at $13.30 (2026-11-06, L)
notes.B48: Pick the 2 NC option; 180 sold, 4.9 stars. Was $13.99 each (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B52: 4.3 stars (682), 50+ bought last month; 5 lb each. Replaces the SoundAlert ($59.99) (2026-11-04, L)
notes.B53: $27.00 is your price in the Sheet (2026-11-06; it was $15.27 + $1.99 on 2026-11-04). 727 sold, 4.9 stars. Amazon: B0DSSZZR5Q $25.99
notes.B54: SKU "1500W 30A": $14.19 + $1.99 shipping, logged-in price; 372 g; size not listed, drawn 130 x 76 x 60 [UNVERIFIED]. The $1.09 1200 W SKU is a welcome price. Amazon: Gebildet potted 12->48 V 6 A B0D66NDXLN $15.99 (2026-11-04, L)

2.title: Borealis Order 2 - materials, LEDs, smoke
rows: SMOKE - custom 12 V fogger (one 200 W core, room for a second), barrel collar, front and rear trail vents
Fog heater core 12 V 200 W, cast heat exchanger 97 x 32 x 36 mm
The fogger: about 17.5 A on its own 30 A PDH channel
Fog fluid pump: Kamoer NKP 12 V peristaltic, 70 mL/min
Feeds the core from the printed tank (a second one comes with a second core)
Core temperature to the main controller (SPI); hold 220-240 C, firmware cut at 245 C
Fluid level: XKC-Y25-NPN non-contact capacitive level switch, 5-12 V
Stuck to the outside of the printed tank at about 20%: low-fluid warning, and the pump stops about a minute later
1-Wire on one controller pin: fogger box by the printed tray (heater off at 70 C), electronics shelf, battery bay; 2 spare
Thermal cutout KSD301 250 C normally closed

Claude: agreed, going to 1/2 in ID ($9.99, rated 200 C). The splitter feeds this line and two 17 mm trail tubes, and the gun's barb has only a 7 mm bore, so as drawn most of the fog would go out the floor vents. A 1/2 in line loses about a quarter of the pressure a 3/8 in one does at the same flow. Heat: the fog is hottest leaving the cores and gets mixed with blower air in the splitter, well under the tube's 200 C (the PETG splitter is the part to watch, not the tube). It stays smoke: it has already condensed into droplets by then, and a wider, slower line loses fewer of them on the wall.
